name: The turnover
note: Rescoped, because the first version had it fertilising and it cannot. Surtsey's gulls fed in the North Atlantic and defecated on the island — an outside, a pump, and a reservoir. A sealed deck has none of those, so animals on it eat on-system and excrete on-system and their net nutrient addition is zero at any stocking density. What they actually do is TURNOVER: eat matter that is locking up, pass it back in a form something else can take, and hold the residence time of a phosphorus atom down to years instead of centuries. In a bag the number that kills you is not how much there is, it is how long it stays unavailable — and this is the building that keeps it moving. Also: peafowl are Phasianidae, the same family as turkeys, and flamingos are filter feeders. Neither is semi-aquatic, neither is a predator, and the first draft of this file called them both both.
